cvEn:
Refael Haiman, son of Lea and Avraham, was born on the 20th of Menachem-Av 5688 (6 August 1928) in Jerusalem to a religious, traditional family. His childhood was spent in the Jewish farming village of Neve Yaakov, after which his family returned to Jerusalem. He completed his elementary schooling at the "Geula" public school in Jerusalem. From his youth he shouldered the burden of work and of supporting the household.

When he finished school, he joined a youth group that went to the Tirat Zvi kibbutz, where he worked as a wagon driver and a field laborer. After the training year, he went with his group to the Gush Etzion bloc to found the Ein Tzurim kibbutz. At first he worked there on land preparation, but he was then sent to Jerusalem to study the trade of driving. From a young age he was a member of the Haganah.

Refael fell on the 28th of Kislev 5708 (11 December 1947). He was among the last defenders of the convoy that was on its way from Jerusalem to the Gush Etzion bloc. He was buried on the Mount of Olives. His name is engraved on the memorial erected in the Military Cemetery on Mount Herzl, in memory of the fallen of the Jewish Quarter and of the fighters who fell in the battle for Jerusalem and were buried on the Mount of Olives.
